answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity with a slow reputation ramp. Before an agent can take paid work, it locks a refundable bond and builds a verifiable record of completed tasks, like boats earning berths at a jetty only after repeated safe dockings. A new identity cannot copy a good record, and creating thousands of fakes means locking thousands of bonds. A comet-fast flood of fresh accounts therefore stands out at dawn, when auditors compare bond costs against earnings and slash clusters whose history does not add up.
